name: Operating System Version
os_min: Windows XP (Source OS historical-update subkeys present on Windows 10+)
purpose: Determines the operating system type, edition, version, and build number, plus installation date(s) for both the currently installed build and any prior builds the system was updated from.
key_fields: ProductName / EditionID - the OS type and edition
DisplayVersion / ReleaseId / CurrentBuildNumber - version and build information
InstallTime - installation time of the current build (64-bit FILETIME, Windows 10+)
InstallDate - installation time of the current build (32-bit Unix epoch)
SYSTEM\Setup\Source OS\<subkey> - one subkey created per historical OS update, holding the same style of ProductName/version/install-time fields for that prior build
normal_baseline: InstallTime/InstallDate consistent with the organization's known imaging or deployment date; ProductName/EditionID matching the licensed SKU on record; Source OS history showing an orderly, expected progression of prior feature updates.
anomalies: InstallTime far more recent than expected for a host believed to be long-lived, consistent with a re-image used to cover tracks or a fresh OS drop tied to an incident
ProductName/EditionID inconsistent with the asset inventory record for that host
Missing or truncated Source OS history where the patch-management record shows multiple feature updates should have occurred
CurrentBuildNumber indicating an outdated/end-of-life build inconsistent with the org's patch-compliance records
InstallTime and InstallDate values that don't correspond to the same moment when converted, suggesting one of the two was altered
anti_forensic_notes: InstallTime reflects the installation time of the CURRENT build only - it is refreshed by feature updates - and does not represent the system's original installation date; the Source OS subkeys must be reviewed together to reconstruct the true build lineage. Timestamps embedded in the Source OS subkey names themselves are extraneous and should not be relied on.
interpretation: CurrentVersion stores ProductName/EditionID (OS type), DisplayVersion/ReleaseId/CurrentBuildNumber (version info), and InstallTime (installation time of the current build, not the original installation). Source OS subkeys are created for each historical OS update and store the same style of information for each prior build. InstallTime is 64-bit FILETIME format (Windows 10+); InstallDate is 32-bit Unix epoch format - both should represent the same moment and can be cross-checked against each other.
